content.stem: NDT personnel certification in Canada is administered by:
options: Natural Resources Canada through the NDTCB
distractors: BINDT administers the PCN scheme in the United Kingdom.
TWI administers CSWIP.
ASNT operates the American schemes.
content.explanation: The Non-Destructive Testing Certification Body within Natural Resources Canada administers certification to the CAN/CGSB-48.9712 standard.

content.stem: The Canadian personnel certification standard is:
options: ISO 9712 as published, with no national adoption
distractors: CSA W178.2 certifies welding inspectors, a different scope.
Canada adopts ISO 9712 through the CGSB standard rather than applying it unmodified.
SNT-TC-1A is the ASNT employer-based recommended practice.
content.explanation: CAN/CGSB-48.9712 is the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712, which is why CGSB certification aligns closely with PCN and CSWIP.

content.stem: Because CAN/CGSB-48.9712 is an adoption of ISO 9712, a CGSB certificate shares with PCN:
options: The three level structure, the three part examination and the five year validity
distractors: The employer based model is SNT-TC-1A, not ISO 9712.
ISO 9712 sets five year validity.
Both schemes certify against defined sectors.
content.explanation: Both are central certification schemes built on ISO 9712, so the level definitions, examination structure and validity match.

content.stem: Certification under CAN/CGSB-48.9712 is granted in respect of:
options: A method, a level and a sector
distractors: Employer independence is a feature of the central scheme.
Certification is national, not provincial.
Validity is five years.
content.explanation: As under ISO 9712, the certificate names method, level and sector, and is independent of the employer.

content.stem: Under the Canadian scheme, weld inspection acceptance is commonly assessed against:
options: CSA W59 for welded steel construction
distractors: ISO 5817 is used in the European framework.
API 1104 governs pipeline welding, a narrower scope.
ASME Section IX qualifies welding procedures and welders, not weld acceptance.
content.explanation: CSA W59 is the Canadian welded steel construction standard and carries the acceptance criteria for structural weld inspection.

content.stem: CSA W178.2 differs from CAN/CGSB-48.9712 in that it certifies:
options: Welding inspectors rather than NDT method personnel
distractors: W178.2 has its own level structure covering more than Level 3.
It is not restricted to radiography.
Procedures are qualified under CSA W47.1 and related standards.
content.explanation: W178.2 certifies welding inspectors. NDT method certification runs under the CGSB standard.

content.stem: A holder of CGSB certification working in the United Kingdom would find that:
options: Recognition depends on the client or employer, since certificates are not automatically interchangeable
The certificate is automatically valid as a PCN certificate
The certificate converts on payment of a fee
distractors: There is no automatic conversion between certification bodies.
Certification is required in both jurisdictions.
Conversion is not a simple fee transaction.
content.explanation: Both schemes derive from ISO 9712, which aids recognition, but acceptance is a matter for the specifying authority rather than automatic.

content.stem: Ionising radiation for industrial radiography in Canada is regulated by:
distractors: The HSE regulates in Great Britain.
The NRC regulates in the United States.
NRCan administers NDT personnel certification, not radiation licensing.
content.explanation: The CNSC licenses and regulates the possession and use of nuclear substances, including industrial radiography sources.

content.stem: Under the Canadian Nuclear Safety and Control Act, an industrial radiographer must hold:
options: Certification as an exposure device operator in addition to NDT certification
distractors: NDT certification does not by itself authorise operation of a radiation exposure device.
Licensing is federal rather than provincial.
Authorisation is required.
content.explanation: Operating an exposure device requires separate CNSC certification, which sits alongside the CGSB NDT certificate.

content.stem: Under CAN/CGSB-48.9712, renewal of certification at five years requires:
options: Evidence of continued work in the method and a current vision record
Full re examination in every case
distractors: Full re examination belongs to recertification.
Evidence of continued activity is required.
Training is required only where activity cannot be shown.
content.explanation: As under ISO 9712, renewal is documentary and recertification at ten years carries the competence demonstration.

content.stem: The vision requirement under the Canadian scheme is:
options: The same annual near vision and colour differentiation test as ISO 9712
distractors: Near vision, not distance vision, is the requirement.
The interval is annual.
The requirement applies in full.
content.explanation: The adoption of ISO 9712 carries its vision requirements across unchanged.

content.stem: Where a Canadian project specifies both CSA W59 and an ISO acceptance standard, the inspector should:
options: Establish which governs by contract before testing and record the basis used
Apply both and report two results
Choose at the time of evaluation
distractors: Selecting the more permissive standard is not a decision the inspector may make.
Two results without a governing basis leave the acceptance undecided.
Deciding at evaluation time is too late and is not auditable.
content.explanation: The governing acceptance basis must be fixed before work starts, otherwise the result cannot be interpreted.
